newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia govt to take over Perwaja's losses-report.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia govt to take over Perwaja's losses-report.

text.p: The Malaysian government will absorb the 2.9 billion ringgit ($1.15 billion) loss posted by national steel firm Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd, newspapers reported on Thursday.
Quoting Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, the Business Times said the government will not pump new money into Perwaja, which is under a new management team led by Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd.
"We are only taking over the losses," Mahathir was quoted as saying on Wednesday.
The government would try to recover the losses from other sources, the national Bernama news agency reported. Mahathir did not elaborate.
Mahathir said under the proposed Perwaja restructuring, the losses would be treated separately as the government wanted the steel firm to start with a clean slate.

Perwaja, a 10-year old pet project of Mahathir's, was found last year to have accumulated losses of 2.9 billion ringgit and its previous government-appointed managers were accused of financial mismanagement.
Mahathir has said the steel project was launched as a government project because steel was a difficult industry and too risky for the private sector.
But the government decided to privatise Perwaja to give its managers more responsibility over the firm's assets.
Mahathir said Maju has been given a 51 percent stake in Perwaja to help in the restructuring and rescue of the steel firm.
He told reporters the Terengganu state government would continue to hold a 19 percent stake in the company and the remaining 30 percent would be held by the federal government.
